claim: WSTS's final full-year 2025 results (released 6 March 2026, incorporating finalised fourth-quarter data) put global semiconductor sales at US$795.6 billion, up 26.2% year over year.
evidence: "Global semiconductor sales reached USD 795.6 billion in 2025, representing an increase of 26.2 percent year-over-year" (WSTS release, 6 Mar 2026); Spring 2026 table: "Total World - $M 795,640 ... 26.2" (WSTS, 2 Jun 2026)

metric.name: Global semiconductor sales
metric.population: WSTS worldwide semiconductor billings (member-reported plus WSTS estimates)
metric.methodology: WSTS shipment statistics, finalised Q4 data

notes: Replaces SIA's preliminary US$791.7bn (Feb 2026) as the 2025 market total. Same value as CLM-0030 (sourced to the Spring 2026 forecast release); this claim cites the results release itself. WSTS segment values in the Spring 2026 table: logic US$299.5bn (+38.8%), memory US$230.0bn (+39.0%).

claim: According to the European Parliamentary Research Service (May 2026), the European Court of Auditors' 2025 special report warned that the EU Chips Act's 20% global market share target for 2030 was unlikely to be achieved, noting the Commission's own forecast projected only 11.7% by 2030.
evidence: "Finally, the ECA warned that the 20 % global market share target by 2030 was unlikely to be achieved, and stressed that the Commission's own forecast projects only 11.7 % by 2030." (EPRS briefing PE 785.742, May 2026, p. 4)

metric.name: Commission forecast of EU share of global semiconductor market
metric.population: EU share of global chip value chain/market as forecast by the Commission (July 2024), as reported by ECA via EPRS
metric.methodology: Commission forecast cited by ECA; reported second-hand by EPRS

notes: Context for CLM-0141. The 11.7% is a Commission forecast reported second-hand; the ECA special report 12/2025 itself was not opened in this run.

claim: On 27 March 1987 President Reagan announced 100% ad valorem duties on as much as US$300 million of Japanese exports, and on 17 April 1987 he proclaimed the Section 301 tariff increases on certain Japanese products, effective for entries on and after that date.
evidence: "On March 27, 1987, I announced my intention to raise customs duties to a level of 100 percent ad valorem on as much as $300 million in Japanese exports"; "The tariff increases I am proclaiming shall be effective with respect to the covered products of Japan which are entered on and after April 17, 1987." (Memorandum, 17 Apr 1987)

metric.name: Ceiling on value of Japanese exports targeted by 1987 retaliatory tariffs
metric.unit: USD million (nominal, upper bound 'as much as')
metric.population: Japanese products targeted for 100% ad valorem duties
